texts.preamble: Khaiser Begum vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 1 November, 2022 Bench: A.Abhishek Reddy, Juvvadi Sridevi The Hon'Ble Sri Justice A.Abhishek Reddy And The Hon'Ble Smt Justice Juvvadi Sridevi Writ Petition No.36523 of 2022 Order:
texts.facts: The case of the petitioner is that basing on five (5) crimes viz., Crime No.112 of 2021 of Chatrinaka Police Station, Crime No.164 of 2021 of Falaknuma Police Station, and Crime Nos.286, 338 and 360 of 2021 of Chandrayangutta Police Station, the respondent No.2 passed the impugned detention order, dated 25.02.2022. According to the respondent No.2, the alleged detenu is a 'Goonda', as, he has been habitually committing burglaries in the limits of Hyderabad Police Commissionerate. He has been causing large scale fear and panic among the general public, thus adversely affecting the public order, peace and tranquility in the area. Subsequently, the impugned detention order was confirmed by the Government vide G.O.Rt.No.1074, dated 21.05.2022.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner would contend that the impugned detention order has been passed in a mechanical manner and without application of mind. Already criminal law was set into motion against the detenu. The impugned detention order was passed on the mere apprehension Khaiser Begum vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 1 November, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12992713/ 1 that the detenu has admitted his guilt in four cases to get away with simple imprisonment and there is every possibility of his admitting guilt in the remaining cases also for securing simple conviction and that after releasing from prison, there is imminent possibility of the detenu indulging in similar prejudicial activities again, which is unjustified. The alleged crimes do not add up to "disturbing the public order" and they are confined within the ambit and scope of the words "law and order". Since the offences alleged are under the Indian Penal Code, the detenu can certainly be tried and convicted thereunder. Thus, there is no need for the detaining authority to invoke the draconian preventive detention law against the detenu. Hence, the impugned orders tantamount to colourable exercise of power. On the other hand, the learned Special Government Pleader appearing for the respondents supported the impugned orders and submitted that the alleged detenu is a 'Goonda' and has been habitually committing burglaries in the limits of Hyderabad Police Commissionerate and thereby acting in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of public order. Therefore, the apprehension of the detaining authority that there is every likelihood of the detenu committing similar offences is not misconceived. The series of crimes allegedly committed by the detenu were sufficient to cause a feeling of insecurity in the minds of the people at large. Therefore, the detaining authority is legally justified in passing the impugned detention order. In catena of cases, the Hon'ble Supreme Court had clearly opined that there is a vast difference between "law and order" and "public order". Hence, according to the Hon'ble Apex Court, the detaining authority should be wary of Khaiser Begum vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 1 November, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12992713/ 2 invoking the immense power under the Act. In Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar1, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has, in fact, deprecated the invoking of the preventive law in order to tackle a law and order problem. It was observed that every breach of public peace and every violation of law may create a 'law and order' problem, but does not necessarily create a problem of 'public order'. 9. In Kanu Biswas v. State of West Bengal2, the Hon'ble Apex Court, while discussing the meaning of word 'public order,' held that the question whether a man has only committed a breach of 'law and order' or has acted in a manner likely to cause a disturbance of the 'public order', is a question of degree and extent of the reach of the act upon the Society.
